# core/p384.bastio

<!-- Generated by tests/libref.py from core/p384.bastio: edit the source, then run tests/libref.py --write. -->

ECDSA signatures over the curve P-384 (secp384r1) with
SHA-384, verification only (FIPS 186-4, RFC 6979 is for signing), for the
ecdsa_secp384r1_sha384 scheme of TLS 1.3 certificates.

What is proved: every access is in bounds, nothing leaks, and the numbers
the arithmetic works on have 24 limbs. Not proved: that the arithmetic is
right; the tests check signatures made by OpenSSL, many one-bit changes of
the signature, key and message being refused, and out-of-range values. The
code is not constant time and does not need to be: verification handles
only public values.

A number is a `Vec[u64]` of 24 limbs of 16 bits, least significant first,
below 2^384. Products are built by doubling and adding, which is slow (a
verification takes about as long as a few thousand field multiplications of
384 steps each) but short enough to read.

`import "core/p384.bastio";` also loads [core/option.bastio](core-option.md), [core/bytes.bastio](core-bytes.md), [core/der.bastio](core-der.md), [core/endian.bastio](core-endian.md), [core/text.bastio](core-text.md), [core/sha512.bastio](core-sha512.md).

| Function | |
| --- | --- |
| [`ecdsa_p384_verify_digest`](#ecdsa_p384_verify_digest) | Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature, under the public key `pubkey` on the curve P-384, of the message whose digest is `digest` (from any hash. |
| [`ecdsa_p384_verify`](#ecdsa_p384_verify) | Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature of `msg` under the public key `pubkey`, with the curve P-384 and SHA-384. |

Every example below is built, verified and run by `tests/run.sh`. An `assert` in one is proved at compile time from the contracts above it.

## Types and constants

### `Modulus384`

```bastio
struct Modulus384 { m: Vec[u64], r2: Vec[u64], minv: u64 }
```

Internal: a prime modulus `m` with what Montgomery multiplication needs:
`r2` is 2^768 modulo `m` and `minv` is -1/m modulo 2^16.

### `P384Point`

```bastio
struct P384Point { x: Vec[u64], y: Vec[u64], z: Vec[u64] }
```

Internal: a point in Jacobian coordinates, (X / Z^2, Y / Z^3); Z = 0 is
the point at infinity.

## Functions

### `ecdsa_p384_verify_digest`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p384_verify_digest(pubkey: &Bytes, digest: &Bytes, sig: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(digest) < 274877906944 && blen(sig) < 274877906944 && blen(pubkey) < 274877906944
```

Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature, under the public key `pubkey`
on the curve P-384, of the message whose digest is `digest` (from any
hash: SHA-256, SHA-384 or SHA-512; a digest longer than 48 bytes is cut
to its leftmost 48; a shorter one is padded with zeros on the left). Encodings as in `ecdsa_p384_verify`.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(97);
let digest = balloc(48);
let sig = balloc(8);
let ok = ecdsa_p384_verify_digest(key, digest, sig);
bfree(sig);
bfree(digest);
bfree(key);
if ok { return 1; }
```

### `ecdsa_p384_verify`

```bastio
fn ecdsa_p384_verify(pubkey: &Bytes, msg: &Bytes, sig: &Bytes) -> bool
  requires blen(msg) < 274877906944 && blen(sig) < 274877906944 && blen(pubkey) < 274877906944
```

Whether `sig` is a valid ECDSA signature of `msg` under the public key
`pubkey`, with the curve P-384 and SHA-384. `pubkey` is the 97 bytes of
an uncompressed point (0x04, x, y) and `sig` the DER encoding of
SEQUENCE { INTEGER r, INTEGER s } that X.509 and TLS use. A key that is
not on the curve, an `r` or `s` outside 1..n-1 and any other encoding are
refused.

Example:

```bastio
let key = balloc(97);
let msg = bfrom("hello");
let sig = balloc(8);
let ok = ecdsa_p384_verify(key, msg, sig);
bfree(sig);
bfree(msg);
bfree(key);
if ok { return 1; }
```

## Specification functions

### `mod384_ok`

```bastio
spec fn mod384_ok(m: &Modulus384) -> bool {
  vlen(m.m) == 24 && vlen(m.r2) == 24
}
```

Internal: the modulus has 24 limbs, like its `r2`.

## Internals

### `p384_nib`

```bastio
fn p384_nib(c: u8) -> u64
  ensures result < 24
```

Internal: the value of the hex digit `c` (0 for anything else).

### `bn384_zero`

```bastio
fn bn384_zero() -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

Internal: the number 0.

### `bn384_copy`

```bastio
fn bn384_copy(a: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 24
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

Internal: a copy of `a`.

### `bn384_small`

```bastio
fn bn384_small(v: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires v < 65536
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

Internal: the number `v` (below 65536).

### `bn384_hex`

```bastio
fn bn384_hex(s: Str) -> Vec[u64]
  requires slen(s) == 96
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

Internal: the number written as the 96 hex digits of `s`.

### `bn384_from_bytes`

```bastio
fn bn384_from_bytes(b: &Bytes, at: u64) -> Vec[u64]
  requires at + 48 <= blen(b) && at < 274877906944
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

Internal: the big-endian number in the 48 bytes `b[at..at+48]`.

### `bn384_ge`

```bastio
fn bn384_ge(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 24 && vlen(b) == 24
```

Internal: whether `a >= b`.

### `bn384_eq`

```bastio
fn bn384_eq(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 24 && vlen(b) == 24
```

Internal: whether `a == b`.

### `bn384_is_zero`

```bastio
fn bn384_is_zero(a: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(a) == 24
```

Internal: whether `a == 0`.

### `bn384_add17`

```bastio
fn bn384_add17(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64]) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 24 && vlen(b) == 24
  ensures vlen(result) == 25
```

Internal: `a + b` modulo 2^384, and in the 25th limb the carry.

### `mod384_add`

```bastio
fn mod384_add(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus384) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 24 && vlen(b) == 24 && mod384_ok(m)
```

### `bn384_bit`

```bastio
fn bn384_bit(a: &Vec[u64], i: u64) -> u64
  requires vlen(a) == 24 && i < 384
  ensures result <= 1
```

### `mont384_mul`

```bastio
fn mont384_mul(a: &Vec[u64], b: &Vec[u64], m: &Modulus384) -> Vec[u64]
  requires vlen(a) == 24 && vlen(b) == 24 && mod384_ok(m)
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

```bastio
fn p384_copy(q: &P384Point) -> P384Point
  requires vlen(q.x) == 24 && vlen(q.y) == 24 && vlen(q.z) == 24
```

### `p384_double`

```bastio
fn p384_double(q: &P384Point, p: &Modulus384) -> P384Point
  requires vlen(q.x) == 24 && vlen(q.y) == 24 && vlen(q.z) == 24 && mod384_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 24 && vlen(result.y) == 24 && vlen(result.z) == 24
```

### `p384_add`

```bastio
fn p384_add(q1: &P384Point, q2: &P384Point, p: &Modulus384) -> P384Point
  requires vlen(q1.x) == 24 && vlen(q1.y) == 24 && vlen(q1.z) == 24
  requires vlen(q2.x) == 24 && vlen(q2.y) == 24 && vlen(q2.z) == 24 && mod384_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 24 && vlen(result.y) == 24 && vlen(result.z) == 24
```

### `p384_mul`

```bastio
fn p384_mul(k: &Vec[u64], q: &P384Point, p: &Modulus384) -> P384Point
  requires vlen(k) == 24 && vlen(q.x) == 24 && vlen(q.y) == 24 && vlen(q.z) == 24 && mod384_ok(p)
  ensures vlen(result.x) == 24 && vlen(result.y) == 24 && vlen(result.z) == 24
```

### `p384_on_curve`

```bastio
fn p384_on_curve(x: &Vec[u64], y: &Vec[u64], p: &Modulus384) -> bool
  requires vlen(x) == 24 && vlen(y) == 24 && mod384_ok(p)
```

Internal: whether (x, y) is on the curve y^2 = x^3 - 3x + b, with both
coordinates below `p`.

### `p384_der_uint`

```bastio
fn p384_der_uint(sig: &Bytes, start: u64, end: u64) -> Option[Bytes]
  requires start <= end && end <= blen(sig)
  ensures result is Option::Some ==> blen(result.Some) == 48
```

Internal: the signature number in the INTEGER `item` of `sig` as 48
bytes, if it is a positive DER integer of at most 384 bits in the shortest
form.

### `p384_verify_numbers`

```bastio
fn p384_verify_numbers(qx: &Vec[u64], qy: &Vec[u64], e: &Vec[u64], r: &Vec[u64], s: &Vec[u64]) -> bool
  requires vlen(qx) == 24 && vlen(qy) == 24 && vlen(e) == 24 && vlen(r) == 24 && vlen(s) == 24
```

Internal: checks the signature (`r`, `s`) of the hash `e` under the key
(`qx`, `qy`), all as numbers.

### `p384_hash_number`

```bastio
fn p384_hash_number(d: &Bytes) -> Vec[u64]
  ensures vlen(result) == 24
```

Internal: the first 48 bytes of the digest `d` (as a number), or `d`
itself with leading zeros when it is shorter (FIPS 186-4 6.4: a longer
hash is cut to the leftmost bits of the order's length).
